topics.title: Clear comparisons with although and because
topics.explanation: Although introduces a contrast. Use although + subject + verb. Do not add but to the same clause pair. Because introduces a reason. Use because + subject + verb; because of is followed by a noun phrase. First correct the example, then translate a sentence, then use the structure in your own argument.

exercises.promptText: Although public transport is cheaper, but some people drive.
options: Although public transport is cheaper, some people drive.
Although public transport is cheaper, but some people drive.
Although public transport cheaper, some people drive.
exercises.correctOption: Although public transport is cheaper, some people drive.
exercises.explanation: Although already marks the contrast, so this sentence does not need but. Both clauses contain a subject and a verb.
exercises.translatePromptUz: Avtobus arzonroq bo‘lsa ham, ba’zi odamlar mashinada yuradi.
exercises.activationPrompt: Write two sentences comparing two ways to travel in your town. Use although to express a real contrast.

exercises.promptText: People cycle because of it saves money.
options: People cycle because it saves money.
People cycle because of it saves money.
exercises.correctOption: People cycle because it saves money.
exercises.explanation: It saves money is a clause with a subject and verb, so use because. Because of needs a noun phrase such as the lower cost.
exercises.translatePromptUz: Men velosipedda yuraman, chunki bu pulimni tejaydi.
exercises.activationPrompt: Explain one choice you made about studying. Use because followed by a complete clause.

topics.title: Talk about routines and changes
topics.explanation: Use the present simple for a routine: I study every evening. Add -s for he/she/it. Use used to + base verb for a past habit that has changed: I used to study alone. In speaking, give a short answer, add a reason, and include a concrete example. Read your completed answer aloud; written grammar checks do not measure pronunciation.

exercises.promptText: My sister study English every evening.
options: My sister studies English every evening.
My sister study English every evening.
My sister studying English every evening.
exercises.correctOption: My sister studies English every evening.
exercises.explanation: My sister is a third-person singular subject. In the present simple, study becomes studies.
exercises.translatePromptUz: Mening opam har oqshom ingliz tilini o‘rganadi.
exercises.activationPrompt: Describe what a family member does on a typical weekday. Say three short sentences, then write the same ideas using the present simple.

exercises.promptText: I used to studied alone, but now I practise with a friend.
options: I used to study alone, but now I practise with a friend.
I used to studied alone, but now I practise with a friend.
I use to studied alone, but now I practise with a friend.
exercises.correctOption: I used to study alone, but now I practise with a friend.
exercises.explanation: Used to is followed by the base form study. It describes a past habit that is different now.
exercises.translatePromptUz: Ilgari men yolg‘iz o‘qirdim, lekin hozir do‘stim bilan mashq qilaman.
exercises.activationPrompt: Describe one habit that has changed since you started learning English. Use used to, explain the change, and read your answer aloud.
